html:
SMTO-ART-0012 — A file copy stopped before it finished

GUID: 1314c02b-aa61-4e61-9386-f5261838ce86
Slug: artifact-transfer-incomplete
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO was copying a file between the computer that ran the Task and the SMTO server, but the copy ended early or stopped moving. The incomplete copy wasn't kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run and look for the file. If it's listed with a Download link, a later attempt already worked and you're done. Checking first avoids saving the same file twice.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway the Task used. The Gateway is the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer. Copies stop early when the connection to that computer drops.
  3. If the file is still missing, select Retry collection in Artifacts from this run if it appears, or ask SMTO in a new message to save the file again. A new copy starts from the beginning of the original file and is checked when it finishes.

What success looks like

  • The file appears once in Artifacts from this run and downloads completely.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again: look in Artifacts from this run first. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep retrying while the Gateway connection is unstable; each attempt starts over from the beginning.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An artifact transfer did not complete: a Gateway chunked read ended before its declared size or returned an empty non-final chunk, or a materialization transfer acknowledged the wrong byte count or failed.

What this means

  • Artifact streaming ends before its declared size or stops advancing, transfer acknowledgement reports the wrong byte offset, or a materialization transfer action returns failure. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact streaming ends before its declared size or stops advancing, transfer acknowledgement reports the wrong byte offset, or a materialization transfer action returns failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original transfer ID, stage and commit evidence before assuming nothing was published.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server and Gateway logs for the transfer diagnostic (ended before the declared size, or no progress) and any transfer_operation failure. Confirm Gateway connectivity and that the source revision is stable, verify in registered_artifacts that no available version already exists, then re-collect through the run's artifacts reconcile endpoint.
  • Inspect and reconcile the original transfer, including any commit attempt, before starting a supported new transfer from the authoritative source.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer is reconciled and a supported complete handoff verifies final size/hash.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
